NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: An elder teaches a treasured recipe, but relatives insist their version is the real one: crown one version, or keep them all.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has decided to teach (subject.his/her) famous coconut fish stew before (subject.he/she) forgets it. Immediately, three relatives, (friend) among them, have said their versions are the real recipe, the way Grandmother made it. They are all different. What should the family do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The family holds a tasting. (subject)'s version wins, narrowly. (friend) insists the judging was unfair. The next week, at (friend)'s hut, there is a suspiciously similar stew, with one extra spice.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) teaches all four versions, side by side, and says Grandmother probably made it differently every time. The family agrees this is likely. Every feast now has four stews, and plenty for the travelers who drop by.
